title: The chowder
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Friday, week one. The chowder is the uncle's recipe from a card in the register. Gully can't read the uncle's hand. Wood can — he's been reading bad handwriting since the postcards. Together they make it wrong and it's right.

panels.composition: The shack. A recipe card, grease-spotted, in the uncle's hand. GULLY squinting. WOOD reading over his shoulder. BARNABY.

balloons.text: That's a three or an eight.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, two teenagers bent over a grease-spotted handwritten recipe card at a shack counter, a small dog beneath

panels.composition: The card. The uncle's hand: slanting, crowded. Wood's finger under a word.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, close-up of a slanting crowded handwritten recipe card with a finger beneath one word
image.notes: The uncle's hand. The strip draws it like Chloe's postcards: crowded, climbing.

panels.composition: The pot. Gully stirring. Wood reading the card aloud, editing, the way he reads postcards to the dog.

balloons.text: '…until it —' something. 'Until it forgives you.' That's what it says.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a teenager stirring a pot while another reads aloud from a card and improvises

panels.composition: A bowl. Gully tasting. The face. Wood waiting.

balloons.text: It's wrong in the same places.
